speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) over the last five years, what is the annual range, median and average commission rates paid by housing developers to their appointed sales agents; and (b) whether the Government is looking to regulate or mandate the disclosure of such commissions paid by property developers.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I see from a February report in The Business Times (BT) where the journalist mentioned that the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) is looking into property agents' commissions and engages developers regularly to obtain information and provide feedback.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: So, I was just wondering if this is something that is going to be of a regular occurrence in terms of collecting commission-related information from developers and whether or not there are plans to then look into the regulation on this?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Or is it mainly a private contractual agreement, as the Minister mentioned?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: In terms of the exact wording, based on what is in the BT article, it was quoted that a URA spokesperson said, "URA does not regulate the commission rates paid by developers to their appointed sales agent.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: As part of our monitoring of the property market, we engage developers regularly to obtain information and provide feedback."

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, the report said that URA does not regulate the commissions.
